name: NVIDIA Rubin (R100/VR200)
disclaimer: Many Rubin figures are GTC 2025/2026 announcements for a GPU not yet shipping at the time of writing (labeled "announced"); die/IO-die/HBM footprints are illustrative and drawn to a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm). Heights, SM grids, DRAM layer counts and the substrate are illustrative.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Multi-layer organic substrate for the Rubin GPU package (announced). Routes power and signals from the four dies and 8 HBM4 stacks to the SXM/board connectors.

components.name: Interposer (CoWoS-L, ~4x reticle)
components.desc: TSMC CoWoS-L interposer, reported at roughly 4x a single reticle to fit two compute dies, two I/O dies and 8 HBM4 stacks.

components.name: Die 0 (compute)
components.desc: One of two near-reticle-sized Rubin compute dies. Holds SMs, L2 slice and memory controllers; NVLink/PCIe SerDes are moved off-die onto a dedicated I/O die to free up area for more SMs. With NVIDIA's Rubin-era counting, each compute die is one "GPU" (so a 72-package NVL72 rack is called NVL144).

specs.label: Process
specs.value: TSMC N3 family (3nm; exact node not confirmed by NVIDIA)

specs.label: Die size
specs.value: near-reticle limit, ~26 x 33 mm (not published; estimate)

components.name: Die 1 (compute)
components.desc: Second Rubin compute die, identical to die 0.

components.name: I/O die (left)
components.desc: Dedicated I/O chiplet carrying the NVLink 6, PCIe and NVLink-C2C SerDes for die 0 — new vs. Blackwell, which puts I/O on the compute die itself. Frees die-0 area for more SMs.

components.name: I/O die (right)
components.desc: Second I/O chiplet, serving die 1.

components.name: Die-to-die link
components.desc: High-bandwidth, coherent link between the two compute dies (successor to NV-HBI). Exact name/bandwidth not disclosed by NVIDIA; software still sees one GPU package.

specs.label: Bandwidth
specs.value: not disclosed (estimate: faster than Blackwell's 10 TB/s NV-HBI)

components.name: Compute-die <-> I/O-die link
components.desc: On-package link carrying NVLink/PCIe traffic between die 0 and its I/O die. Illustrative — NVIDIA has not published this interconnect's name or bandwidth.

components.name: Compute-die <-> I/O-die link
components.desc: Same link for die 1 and its I/O die.

components.name: HBM4 base die
components.desc: Logic base die at the bottom of each HBM4 stack: the PHY that talks to the memory controller through the interposer.

components.name: HBM4 DRAM layers
components.desc: Stacked HBM4 DRAM dies joined by TSVs. 4 of the package's 8 stacks sit on this side, beyond the I/O die, feeding die 0. LLM decoding is usually bound by this bandwidth: every token re-reads the weights.

components.name: HBM4 base die
components.desc: Logic base die at the bottom of each HBM4 stack, feeding die 1.

components.name: HBM4 DRAM layers
components.desc: Stacked HBM4 DRAM dies joined by TSVs, feeding die 1.

components.name: L2 cache (die 0)
components.desc: Shared L2 cache slice, coherent across both compute dies. Buffers data between HBM4 and all SMs; hot weights and KV cache stay here instead of round-tripping to HBM. Size not disclosed by NVIDIA.

components.name: L2 cache (die 1)
components.desc: Shared L2 cache slice on die 1.

components.name: Memory controllers (die 0)
components.desc: Memory controllers + HBM4 PHY: turn read/write requests into signals for the 4 HBM4 stacks beyond the I/O die on this side.

components.name: Memory controllers (die 1)
components.desc: Memory controllers + HBM4 PHY for die 1.

components.name: NVLink 6 / PCIe (via I/O die)
components.desc: Off-chip I/O, physically routed through the adjacent I/O die. NVLink 6 connects GPUs through NVSwitch in the NVL72/NVL144 rack; NVLink-C2C connects the Vera CPU.

components.name: NVLink 6 / PCIe (via I/O die)
components.desc: Off-chip I/O ports on die 1, routed through its I/O die.

components.name: SMs (die 0)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors — the basic compute unit. 224 SMs total across the package (announced); this grid is symbolic. Click **Open SM** to look inside.

specs.label: SM count
specs.value: 224 total on package (announced); grid below is symbolic

components.name: SMs (die 0)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: SMs (die 1)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: SMs (die 1)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: L1 / Shared memory
components.desc: Programmable scratchpad shared by the threads of a block. TMA fills it with A/B tiles; Tensor Cores read operands straight from here. Size not disclosed for Rubin.

specs.label: Size (per SM)
specs.value: not disclosed; estimate similar order to Blackwell's ~256 KB

components.name: Tensor Memory (TMEM)
components.desc: Dedicated memory where Tensor Cores keep accumulators instead of registers, carried over from Blackwell. Frees registers for other work and allows larger matmul tiles.

specs.label: Size (per SM)
specs.value: not disclosed for Rubin; estimate similar order to Blackwell's 256 KB

components.name: Rubin Tensor Core
components.desc: Multiplies whole matrix tiles per instruction, now with native NVFP4 and a 3rd-generation Transformer Engine (adaptive, two-level micro-block scaling). NVIDIA's own materials describe it as an enhanced 5th-generation Tensor Core; several press reports call it 6th-gen — treat the generation number as unsettled.

specs.label: Tensor Core generation
specs.value: NVIDIA: enhanced 5th-gen; several press reports: 6th-gen (unsettled naming)

specs.label: NVFP4 effective/inference (per GPU package)
specs.value: up to 50 PFLOPS via 3rd-gen Transformer Engine sparsity (announced)

components.name: Register file
components.desc: Per-thread registers — the fastest storage. One slice per SM sub-partition.

specs.label: Size (per SM)
specs.value: not disclosed; estimate similar order to Blackwell

components.name: Warp scheduler + CUDA cores
components.desc: Each cycle picks a ready warp (32 threads) to issue. Scalar CUDA cores run the epilogue: bias, activation, quantization. NVIDIA cites dedicated softmax acceleration at 32 ops/clock/SM (FP32) and 64 ops/clock/SM (FP16) for attention workloads.

components.name: TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator)
components.desc: Copies whole multi-dimensional tensor tiles between L2/HBM4 and shared memory asynchronously, without spending threads.

steps.text: 1. Weights W and activations X sit in HBM4.
2. A memory controller reads the HBM4 stacks attached to its die, through the interposer beyond the I/O die.
3. If the data lives in the other die's HBM4, it crosses the die-to-die link — invisible to software, both dies behave as one GPU package.
4. Data lands in the shared L2 cache.
5. TMA copies A and B tiles from L2 into shared memory, asynchronously.
6. Tiles sit in shared memory, ready for the Tensor Cores.
7. The Rubin Tensor Cores multiply the tiles natively in NVFP4 (micro-block scaled), with the 3rd-gen Transformer Engine adjusting precision per layer.
8. Partial sums accumulate in TMEM, not in registers. Steps 5-8 repeat along K.
9. Epilogue: results move TMEM -> registers; CUDA cores add bias, apply activation (softmax accel for attention), quantize back to NVFP4.
10. Results go back to HBM4 via TMA; with tensor parallelism, NVLink 6 (3.6 TB/s, through the I/O die) all-reduces with other GPUs in the NVL72/NVL144 rack.

summary.value: ~858 mm² per compute die (reticle limit; estimate, not published)
TSMC N3 family (3nm; exact node unconfirmed)
~1,800 W per Rubin GPU (NVIDIA datasheet power assumption for Vera Rubin NVL4)
17.5 PFLOPS dense FP8/FP6 (training spec), per Rubin GPU
4,000 TFLOPS dense FP16/BF16 (4 PFLOPS), per Rubin GPU
2,000 TFLOPS dense TF32 (2 PFLOPS), per Rubin GPU
19.2 TB/s per Rubin GPU (Vera Rubin NVL72 spec; launch blog said 'up to 22 TB/s')
3,000 GB/s per GPU (NVLink 6; current datasheet, launch blog said 3.6 TB/s)
1,800 GB/s bidirectional NVLink-C2C to Vera CPU

scale.basis: Compute die ~= 26 x 33 mm (reticle limit, estimate); I/O die and HBM4 stack footprints estimated
